description: minimumReleaseAge is the point of this file. The committed .terraform.lock.hcl stops silent provider upgrades; this is what keeps them flowing anyway, just late enough that someone else finds the bugs first.

aws 6.57.0 (2026-07-29) broke every data-source read across services and was reported within four hours. A soak window would not have delayed us - it would have skipped that build entirely and landed us on the fix release.

packageRules.description: Providers are the fleet-wide blast radius: one bad release reaches every stack that inits. One PR per provider, so a bad bump reverts without dragging unrelated updates with it.

Terraform MODULE bumps change resource shape and can force replacements. The rds module is pinned deliberately - v6 dropped db_instance_password, see terraform/physical/CLAUDE.md. These need a human reading the plan, so never open them automatically.
The Go harness in live/tests ships to nobody and release-please excludes it, so its dependencies can move on a shorter soak.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes skip the soak. The reason to wait is that other people have not found the bugs yet, and that reasoning inverts once the bug is known and being exploited.
